reference_change.title: Write number text directly as ASCII bytes in `UTF8JsonGenerator`

workload.source: written here from the description of https://github.com/FasterXML/jackson-core/pull/1706, whose harness is not in the tree: a program writing 30-digit BigDecimals (their text cached) through UTF8JsonGenerator with USE_FAST_DOUBLE_WRITER off, in process, warmed up until stable (eval/tasks/workloads/fasterxml-jackson-core-pr1706/NumberWriteWorkload.java). In single runs on JDK 21 (macOS arm64), the last warm-up iterations in the recorded workload output took about 16 ms on the task tree and 16 to 20 ms on the reference tree; that is one run each, and no conclusion is drawn from it. The description's own table (JDK 17, another harness, an earlier form of the loop) shows the copy path halved.

oracle.source: GeneratorBasicTest, the test class https://github.com/FasterXML/jackson-core/pull/1706 extends; targeted tests only

evidence.note: description: number text is written as ASCII bytes straight into the output buffer; a hand-rolled harness with 5 JVM forks is quoted

status_reason: built here, and the oracle ran on the task and reference trees (see runs); the workload was run too, but only in an earlier form (below). Built with the project's Maven wrapper and the JDK on the PATH (Eclipse Temurin 21). The workload ran; the recorded tails do not settle whether this change is faster, so that is open: labelling decides what the task is worth. The workload runs recorded here predate the warm-up rule now in the committed workload (a floor of 200 iterations, 1% tolerance, a cap of 600 that reports instead of failing); the iteration bodies are unchanged, but the program that ran is not the committed one, so workload.verified is false until it is run again on a quiet machine.
